competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move under the trusted duration-1 P&L convention. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

performance_reflections.what_happened_vs_expected: The oil-supported CADJPY long was expected to keep overnight relative-value standing stable; instead competition rank moved from 8 to 12 with about 67780 of net and drawdown while the live long is still above the 110.90 entry and the Australia-Canada cash wedge is unchanged.

causal.original_belief: A CADJPY long that isolates Canada's oil surplus against Japan's energy-import bill would keep overnight relative-value performance competitive without needing a fresh Australia-Canada trade.
causal.observed_reality: Rank slipped from 8 to 12 with about 67780 of net and drawdown even as CADJPY prints 111.59 above 110.90 and AONIA 4.60 versus CORRA 2.27 shows no new Australia-Canada policy, growth, or inflation shock.
causal.assumptions_right: Crude still prices Canada as the surplus exporter and Japan as the importer, so the live CADJPY mark continues to transmit the intended terms-of-trade gap.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Competition rank can fall from residual path in already-closed AUDCAD expressions and from peers harvesting dollar-directional beta even while the Canada-Japan oil differential is paying.
causal.causal_divergence: The rank move and 67780 drawdown score closed Australia-Canada residuals and peer-relative P&L, not a reversal in the oil-supported Canada-versus-Japan cross that is still above entry.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same oil tape, the same AONIA-CORRA wedge, and the same 111.59 CADJPY print, cutting the working long or reversing the closed AUDCAD fade would have added expression noise rather than repaired rank.
causal.future_implication: A competition rank drop is not a new Australia-versus-Canada policy, growth, or inflation gap and must not reopen faded AUDCAD or replace CADJPY with a dollar pair.

performance_reflections.no_new_lesson: The 8-to-12 rank move and 67780 drawdown are the leaderboard echo of already-closed Australia-Canada fades plus peer-relative scoring; they sit inside ordinary competition variance around an intact oil-supported CADJPY differential, so the original process remains sound: hold the working Canada-Japan cross and leave the closed fade shut on a known cash gap.
